newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAB SEES BETTER ATTRIB INCOME THIS YEAR.
newsitem.headline: SAB SEES BETTER ATTRIB INCOME THIS YEAR.

text.p: South African Breweries Ltd said on Tuesday it expected real growth in attributable earnings for the current year.
"SAB is budgeting for real growth in attributable earnings, with growth in earnings per share inevitably tempered by the increased number of shares in issue," it said in a statement.

SAB said its focus on mass consumer markets positioned it uniquely to capitalise on a resurgence in private consumption and that this, together with the prospect of an easing in local interest rates later in the year, would eable it to grow earnings.

The outlook for South Africa's economy and consumer spending remained relatively subdued but responsible fiscal and economic policies and a more stable rand should underpin current modest growth levels, the world's fourth largest brewer said.
"However, a meaningful upturn in consumer spending cannot be expected until real interest rates decline, private household debt reduces and consumer confidence returns," it said.
